answer_1.quote: Automatic chart summarization is a task where the goal is to explain a chart and summarize key takeaways from it in natural language.

answer_2.quote: For automatic evaluation of the summary quality, we utilized five measures. BLEU and CIDEr measure n-gram overlaps between the model generated text and the reference text.

answer_4.quote: To further assess the summary quality we performed a human evaluation on 150 randomly sampled charts from the Statista dataset with four internal annotators who are native speakers of English.
answer_4.guideline: They compared the summaries based on three criteria: (i) Factual correctness: Which summary is more factually correct (i.e., facts mentioned are supported by the chart)? (ii) Coherence: Which summary is more coherent (i.e., sentences are well connected)? and (iii) Fluency: Which summary is more fluent and grammatically correct?
